title: Pappa al Pomodoro
author: Marco Bellini
desc: A thick, comforting Tuscan bread and tomato soup, stale bread simmered directly into ripe tomatoes and basil until it breaks down into a rustic, spoonable porridge-like texture.
longDesc: Pappa al pomodoro reflects the same no-waste Tuscan philosophy behind ribollita and panzanella, transforming day-old bread and summer's ripest tomatoes into something greater than the sum of its humble parts.
ingredients: 300 g (10.5 oz) stale rustic bread, torn into chunks
1 kg (2.2 lb) ripe tomatoes, or 800g (28oz) canned crushed tomatoes
100 ml (scant 1/2 cup) extra virgin olive oil, plus more for serving
steps: If using fresh tomatoes, blanch, peel, and roughly chop them.
Warm the olive oil in a large pot and gently saute the garlic until fragrant, taking care not to brown it.
Add the tomatoes and simmer for 15-20 minutes until they break down into a thick sauce.
Add the stock and bring to a gentle simmer.
Stir in the torn bread and cook, stirring frequently, for 10-15 minutes until it fully breaks down and thickens the soup to a porridge-like consistency.
Stir in torn basil, season to taste, and let rest for a few minutes off the heat.
Serve warm or at room temperature, with a generous drizzle of olive oil.
chefTips: Genuinely stale, sturdy bread breaks down the best into the right thick, cohesive texture.
The best pappa al pomodoro depends heavily on ripe, flavorful tomatoes when made fresh in summer.
This dish is traditionally served warm or even at room temperature, not piping hot, and is excellent the next day.
commonMistakes: Using fresh, soft bread, which does not break down properly into the traditional thick, cohesive texture.
Rushing the tomato cooking time, leaving them not fully broken down into a rich sauce.
Skimping on the olive oil, which is essential both during cooking and as a finishing touch.
servedWith: A drizzle of good olive oil at the table
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; flavor improves the next day.
reheating: Reheat gently on the stovetop, adding a little water or stock if too thick.
healthBenefits: Tomatoes provide lycopene and vitamin C; a naturally vegan, plant-based dish.
culturalNote: Pappa al pomodoro exemplifies Tuscany's resourceful cucina povera tradition, transforming stale bread and ripe summer tomatoes into one of the region's most beloved comfort dishes.
